what_happened: The UK Parliament enacted the Explosive Substances Act 1883.
The FBI's official history dates the founding of the federal investigative agency that became the FBI to 1908.
MI5 states that it has existed in different forms since 1909, beginning as the Secret Service Bureau.
A bomb exploded on Wall Street; the FBI's history page states that those responsible were not identified.
King Alexander I of Yugoslavia was assassinated; the Library of Congress record states that France then proposed a League of Nations convention on terrorism.
The League of Nations adopted the Convention for the Prevention and Punishment of Terrorism; the Library of Congress record states it never came into effect.
The Oireachtas enacted the Offences against the State Act, 1939.
The Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft was concluded.
The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft was concluded.
The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation was concluded.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 3034 (XXVII) on measures to prevent international terrorism.
The UK Parliament enacted the Northern Ireland (Emergency Provisions) Act 1973.

what_happened: The Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons was adopted.
The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1974.
The Council of Europe's European Convention on the Suppression of Terrorism (ETS No. 090) was opened for signature (source page not machine-readable; see sources.csv).

what_happened: The Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material was opened for signature.

what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 40/61 on measures to prevent international terrorism.

what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 579 (1985) on hostage-taking and abduction.
France enacted Loi n° 86-1020 relative à la lutte contre le terrorisme.
The Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts of Violence at Airports Serving International Civil Aviation was concluded.
The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Maritime Navigation was concluded.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in Brogan and Others v. the United Kingdom concerning detention under prevention-of-terrorism legislation.
Pan Am Flight 103 was destroyed by a bomb over Lockerbie, according to the FBI's history page.
The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1989.

The G7 established the Financial Action Task Force to address money laundering, according to the FATF's history page.
The Convention on the Marking of Plastic Explosives for the Purpose of Detection was concluded.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 748 (1992) imposing measures on Libya.
A bomb exploded in the parking garage of the World Trade Center, according to the FBI's history page.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 49/60 containing the Declaration on Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism.
The Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building was bombed; the FBI's history page records 168 deaths.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in McCann and Others v. the United Kingdom concerning the 1988 Gibraltar shootings.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1044 (1996) concerning Sudan and the attempted assassination of President Mubarak in Addis Ababa.
The US Congress enacted the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 51/210, which established an Ad Hoc Committee on international terrorism conventions.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings was adopted.
The Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement was concluded.
The Arab Convention for the Suppression of Terrorism was concluded under the League of Arab States.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1189 (1998) after the bombings in Nairobi and Dar-es-Salaam.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1192 (1998) on a trial in the Netherlands relating to the Pan Am 103 bombing.
The OAU Convention on the Prevention and Combating of Terrorism was adopted (date as given on the AU treaty page; see NOTES.md).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1267 (1999), establishing a sanctions regime and committee concerning the Taliban.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1269 (1999) on international terrorism.

what_happened: The International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism was adopted.
The UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2000.

place: New York, Washington D.C. and Pennsylvania, United States
what_happened: Hijacked aircraft struck the World Trade Center and the Pentagon and crashed in Pennsylvania; the attacks are examined in the 9/11 Commission Report.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1368 (2001) condemning the 11 September attacks.
The North Atlantic Council stated that, if the attack was directed from abroad, it would be regarded as an action covered by Article 5 of the Washington Treaty.
The Authorization for Use of Military Force (Pub. L. 107-40) was enacted.
Executive Order 13224 on blocking property of designated persons was issued.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1373 (2001), which established the Counter-Terrorism Committee.
The USA PATRIOT Act (Pub. L. 107-56) was enacted.
The FATF issued Eight Special Recommendations on terrorist financing, according to its history page.
The US President issued a Military Order on detention, treatment and trial of certain non-citizens.
The UK Parliament enacted the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001, including detention powers in Part 4.
Canada's Anti-terrorism Act (S.C. 2001, c. 41) was enacted; the exact assent date is not shown on the fetched page.
The Inter-American Convention against Terrorism was adopted by the OAS.
The Council of the EU adopted Framework Decision 2002/475/JHA on combating terrorism.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1438 (2002) condemning the bombings in Bali.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1440 (2002) condemning the hostage-taking in Moscow.
The Homeland Security Act of 2002 was enacted, establishing the Department of Homeland Security.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1450 (2002) condemning attacks in Kenya.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1465 (2003) condemning a bombing in Bogota.
The Terrorist Threat Integration Center opened, according to NCTC's history page.
The DOJ Office of the Inspector General released its review of the treatment of immigration detainees held in connection with the September 11 investigation.
Peru's Truth and Reconciliation Commission (CVR) issued its final report covering 1980-2000; the release date is not printed on the fetched page.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1516 (2003) condemning bombings in Istanbul.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1530 (2004) condemning the Madrid train bombings; the resolution's text attributed them to ETA (see NOTES.md on this attribution).

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1535 (2004), establishing the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1540 (2004) on non-state actors and weapons of mass destruction.
The US Supreme Court decided Rasul v. Bush on federal court jurisdiction over habeas petitions from Guantanamo detainees.
The US Supreme Court decided Hamdi v. Rumsfeld on due process for a US citizen detained as an enemy combatant.
The National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States released the 9/11 Commission Report.
Executive Order 13354 incorporated TTIC into the National Counterterrorism Center, according to NCTC's history page.
Definitions differ: Security Council resolution 1566 (2004) describes terrorist acts in its own wording, while the 1937 League of Nations convention used a different definition.

Positions differed on Part 4 detention powers: the UK government had enacted them in the 2001 Act, and the House of Lords in A v Secretary of State held the related provision incompatible with the European Convention on Human Rights.
The Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 was enacted.
The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism Act 2005 (control orders).

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism was adopted.

place: Geneva, Switzerland (UN Commission on Human Rights)
what_happened: The UN Commission on Human Rights adopted resolution 2005/80, creating a Special Rapporteur on human rights while countering terrorism (source text not machine-verified).
The Council of Europe Convention on the Prevention of Terrorism (CETS No. 196) was opened for signature (source page not machine-readable).
Bombs exploded on London's transport system; the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1611 (2005) the same day.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1624 (2005) on incitement to commit terrorist acts.
The Council of the EU issued the European Union Counter-Terrorism Strategy (document 14469/4/05 REV 4).
The UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2006.

Positions differed on military commissions: the 2001 Military Order created them, and the US Supreme Court in Hamdan v. Rumsfeld held that the military commission convened to try Hamdan lacked power to proceed.

place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted the United Nations Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy (A/RES/60/288).
The Military Commissions Act of 2006 was enacted.
ASEAN member states concluded the ASEAN Convention on Counter Terrorism.
The DOJ Office of the Inspector General issued its review of the FBI's use of National Security Letters, as directed by the 2005 PATRIOT Act reauthorization.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1757 (2007) concerning the Special Tribunal for Lebanon.

Positions differed on habeas corpus for Guantanamo detainees: the Military Commissions Act of 2006 restricted it, and the US Supreme Court in Boumediene v. Bush held detainees have the constitutional privilege of habeas corpus.

Positions differed on implementing UN sanctions listings: the Court of Justice in Kadi annulled the EU regulation as it concerned the applicants, on fundamental-rights grounds, while the UN 1267 listing regime continued.
Executive Order 13491 on ensuring lawful interrogations was issued.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The ECtHR Grand Chamber delivered judgment in A. and Others v. the United Kingdom on detention under the 2001 Act.
The Intelligence and Security Committee published 'Could 7/7 Have Been Prevented?', its review of intelligence on the 7 July 2005 attacks.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1904 (2009), creating the Office of the Ombudsperson for the Al-Qaida sanctions list.
The US Supreme Court decided Holder v. Humanitarian Law Project on the material-support statute.
The UN Special Rapporteur on counter-terrorism and human rights issued report A/HRC/16/51 on ten areas of best practices.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)

The White House issued the National Strategy for Counterterrorism.
The UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures Act 2011.
Norway's 22 July Commission delivered its report (NOU 2012: 14) on the 22 July 2011 attacks in Oslo and on Utøya.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The ECtHR Grand Chamber delivered judgment in El-Masri v. the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.
The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board issued its report on the Section 215 telephone records program.

place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
what_happened: The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in Al Nashiri v. Poland.

The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence released the executive summary of its study of the CIA detention and interrogation program, published together with additional and minority views.
The UK Parliament enacted the Counter-Terrorism and Security Act 2015.
The USA FREEDOM Act of 2015 was enacted.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2253 (2015), renaming the regime the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions list.
Brazil enacted Lei nº 13.260 (anti-terrorism law) (source page not machine-verified).
Directive (EU) 2017/541 on combating terrorism was adopted.

place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2349 (2017) on the Lake Chad Basin region.
The US Government Accountability Office published report GAO-17-300 on federal countering violent extremism efforts.

what_happened: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 71/291, establishing the Office of Counter-Terrorism.

what_happened: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2359 (2017) welcoming the deployment of the G5 Sahel Joint Force.
France enacted Loi n° 2017-1510 renforçant la sécurité intérieure et la lutte contre le terrorisme.

Two mosques in Christchurch were attacked; a Royal Commission of Inquiry later reported on the attack (26 November 2020).

The DOJ Office of the Inspector General issued its review of four FISA applications.
The United States and the Taliban signed the Agreement for Bringing Peace to Afghanistan.
The Philippines enacted Republic Act No. 11479, the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020 (source page not machine-verified).
The National Security Council issued the National Strategy for Countering Domestic Terrorism.
